questions.question: Which THREE words in the definition of a business cycle carry its meaning?
options: Successive, real and trend — phases in fixed order, measured in real GDP, around a long-term growth path

questions.question: Starting from the lowest point of the cycle, the phases follow in the order:
On the cycle diagram, the LENGTH of a cycle is measured as:
options: The vertical distance from trend line to peak
The slope of the trend line
The time from one peak to the next peak, or trough to trough
The depth of the deepest recession

questions.question: A large AMPLITUDE tells you that:
options: The economy is at its trough
The shock behind the cycle was strong and its effects will take longer to fade

subtopics.title: Why Cycles Happen — Causes and Types

questions.question: Drought, wars, oil shocks and pandemics as causes of the cycle are examples of:
options: Exogenous explanations — causes located outside the market system
Endogenous explanations — causes inside the market

questions.question: According to the monetarists, the biggest single disturber of the economy is:
options: Government itself — erratic money supply growth and politically timed budgets

questions.question: The Keynesian account of a self-feeding upswing runs through:
options: Rising confidence, investment, the multiplier and the accelerator reinforcing one another

questions.question: Ordered from shortest to longest, the four named cycle types are:
options: Kitchin, Juglar, Kuznets, Kondratieff — inventories, machinery, building, technology

subtopics.title: Leaning Against the Wave — Monetary and Fiscal Policy

questions.question: The repo rate is:
options: The rate at which the Reserve Bank lends to commercial banks — its main monetary policy lever
The rate of VAT on essential goods
The interest rate on government bonds only
The fee for opening a bank account

questions.question: Selling government securities to soak cash out of the banking system is called:
The repo cut to a record low of 3,5 percent in 2020 was an example of:
options: Contractionary monetary policy at the peak
Expansionary monetary policy in a downswing — cheap credit to carry the economy across the trough

questions.question: Progressive income tax and UIF payouts are called AUTOMATIC stabilisers because they:
options: Are adjusted by Parliament every quarter
Are set by the Reserve Bank
Cushion the cycle without any new decision — tax takes less as incomes fall, payouts rise as jobs are lost

subtopics.title: The New Economic Paradigm and Reading the Future

questions.question: The new economic paradigm pairs:
options: Moderate, predictable demand-side policy with supply-side measures that raise capacity
Zero government spending with a fixed exchange rate

questions.question: Smoothing the cycle under the new paradigm means:
options: Narrowing the amplitude while supply-side reform lifts the trend

questions.question: New manufacturing orders, building plans passed and confidence surveys are watched because they are:
options: Lagging indicators that confirm the past
Coincident indicators moving with the tills
Leading indicators — they tend to bend months before the economy follows

questions.question: A moving average is useful in forecasting because it:
options: Removes the trend from a series
Doubles the amplitude of the cycle
Averages each period with its neighbours, filtering out noise so the direction shows

questions.question: The mine on skeleton shifts, empty hostel beds, and nothing getting worse anymore — the town is at:
options: The trough — the lowest point, where activity has stopped falling

questions.question: The recalled shift's wages are spent at the taxi rank and shisanyama, and those takings get spent again. This is:
options: The multiplier running upward through the town

questions.question: Overtime on every roster, no spare boilermaker at any wage, rents jumping — the town is at:
options: The peak — output cannot rise further and the strain shows up as rising prices

questions.question: In the town's picture, the wave, the slope and the swing away from the slope are respectively:
options: The budget, the repo rate and the deficit
The business cycle, the long-term trend, and the amplitude

questions.question: Calling the repo rate a thermostat means:
options: Dial down to heat spending with cheaper borrowing; dial up to cool spending when prices sprint
It controls the temperature in the mines
It moves automatically with the weather

questions.question: The repo hikes of 2022 and 2023 were the dial turned:
options: Up, to cool spending and slow inflation that had escaped the target band

questions.question: The retrenched welder stops paying income tax and starts drawing UIF, so his family's spending falls by less than his wage. This shows:
options: That monetary policy caused the retrenchment
The safety net working as an automatic shock absorber, with nobody deciding anything

questions.question: "Neither lever can mine an ounce of platinum or generate a megawatt" is the point that:
options: The Reserve Bank owns the mines
Fiscal policy is stronger than monetary policy
Demand-side tools cannot repair a supply-side fault — money queues behind the flooded shaft or dead substation

subtopics.title: Reading the Signs Before the Wave Turns

questions.question: Equipment orders placed by the mine and house plans lodged at the municipality are:
options: Leading indicators — actions taken today because of what people expect tomorrow

questions.question: The mine converting contractors to permanent staff only months after recovery began mirrors which national series?
options: Unemployment, a lagging indicator that keeps rising after the trough has passed

questions.question: Extrapolation fails at exactly the turning point because it:
options: Needs too much data to compute
Projects the current path forward, and a turning point is precisely where the path changes

questions.question: "Narrow the amplitude, raise the trend" is a one-line summary of:
options: The case for abolishing monetary policy
The Keynesian rejection of supply-side reform
A plan for permanent maximum stimulus
The new paradigm — steady demand-side policy to keep swings small, plus supply-side measures to lift the growth path
